_comment: Hand-authored input to scripts/build-presentation.mjs. Covers what changelog.json never recorded, the impact line for every row, and the demo each row opens. A row with a `version` takes its detail bullets from that changelog entry; a row without one carries its own. Delete a supplement row if its capability ever gets a real changelog entry (ADR 0022).
title: What shipped since 21 September

headline.title: The SOR window: pick a layout
headline.impact: Eight candidate layouts for the SOR window, switchable from a bar at the bottom of any SOR. Open the demo SOR, try them, and pick one. How an SOR works does not change.

headline.title: Revert to last stage; Resume or Start fresh
headline.impact: A move can be taken back one step, even from Closed Lost. Coming back to a Stage asks whether to pick up the earlier work or start again, and tasks from a Stage the SOR has left wait on hold instead of cluttering lists.

headline.title: Always sees: Everyone · Always edits · Legacy Pipeline open
headline.impact: Each Sales Flow says who always sees its SORs, now including Everyone, and who always edits them. Legacy Pipeline is open to everyone, as before Sales Flows; Government and Outright stay private.
changes: Always sees and Journey viewers can be set to Everyone, and the Flow Canvas shows it on every Stage's audience.
New Always edits list per flow: the people named there can edit every SOR of that Sale Type, the way the Deal Team can.
Legacy Pipeline's Always sees and Always edits are both Everyone, so the SORs registered before Sales Flows behave as they always did.
The SOR window asks the database whether you can edit, so the Edit button and what the database allows always agree.
Every employee can edit the Flow Canvas again; saving a Stage no longer fails with a database permission error.

headline.title: Settings in tabs, saved task filters
headline.impact: Settings is six tabs, and you only see the ones you can use. Leave categories moved into Settings. On Tasks, Save filters as default remembers every filter.
changes: Settings is split into tabs: General, Approval Rules, HR & Schedule, Sales Configuration, Employee Groups and System Announcements. You only see the tabs you can use.
Leave categories are managed in Settings, under HR & Schedule. HR Management has a card that takes you there.
Changing an approval rule takes effect in open approval queues straight away, with no page reload.
On Tasks, "Save filters as default" remembers every filter, not just SORS.
On Tasks and Group Tasks the button reads "Default saved" once saved, or "Update default" if the filters changed since.
Task windows lead with the title and description, then the task itself.
The Commission Pool card in Settings opens with the keyboard.

headline.title: One-row SORS header, floating Register button
headline.impact: Search and figures on the left, view tabs and Filters on the right, all on one row that no longer shifts when you switch views. Register SOR is a floating button at the bottom right.

headline.title: One consistent look
headline.impact: Pick-lists, form fields, tables, pop-ups and side panels look and behave the same on every screen, with keyboard support everywhere.

underTheHood.summary: Fixes you would only notice by their absence. Each one shows the same screen before and after.

items.title: An SOR's Product List, and its Estimated Value, could double
Opening an SOR no longer logs a false "Added product(s)"
An SOR on a Sales Flow's Closed Lost leaves the commission pool
Registering an SOR no longer asks for the first Stage's assignments
An empty register shows its empty state on the Board too

epics.title: SORS register
epics.unlocks: The register stops being a list and becomes the place the commercial process is run from.

epics.title: SOR modal organised around the Stage Visit
epics.unlocks: Opening an SOR shows what this Stage needs now, what already happened, what is being sold, and the conversation, instead of one long form.

epics.title: Stage-scoped SOR visibility
epics.unlocks: A purchaser or engineer called into one Stage sees that Stage and nothing else, and some Stages can be closed to some of the Deal Team. Enforced by the database (ADR 0021).

epics.title: Revert to last stage, and Resume or Start fresh on a Return
epics.unlocks: A wrong move can be taken back, and a Stage visited twice asks what to do with the work already done there.

epics.title: SOR History shows each visit's whole Stage Work
epics.unlocks: Every pass through a Stage keeps its evidence, fields, follow-ups, actions and tasks, readable after the SOR moves on.

epics.title: Sales and Purchasing coordinate buying per SOR
epics.unlocks: Sales raises a Purchase Request from the SOR, Purchasing works it in a queue, and the SOR reads back what is being bought. Retires the old purchasing surfaces.

epics.title: Purchasing and Finance record, approve and file each Odoo purchase order
epics.unlocks: One Odoo purchase order end to end in one record - supplier, payments, charges, landed cost, documents, sign-offs and filing.

epics.title: Costing Matrix
epics.unlocks: Sales, Purchasing and Management cost a bid in the ERP instead of in a spreadsheet, with the Evaluation of Specification beside it.

epics.title: Canvass and Offers
epics.unlocks: Purchasing compares suppliers per Component, and the winning offer fills the Costing Matrix.

epics.title: Transmittals (TG03) and Packing Lists
epics.unlocks: Goods checked by the Warehouse and Technical, and packed boxes on record, following the real TG03 paper form.

epics.title: Order Monitoring
epics.unlocks: What needs doing across every IPAS, with the order register behind it and ageing rules Purchasing edits.

prototypes.title: Printed IPAS
prototypes.note: The IPAS as it would be printed and filed. Sections follow the sheet - 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, with section 4 removed.

prototypes.title: Printed Costing Matrix
prototypes.note: The costing sheet on paper - Components, bundles, inclusions, markup and the summary.

prototypes.title: Printed Canvass
prototypes.note: Supplier offers compared per Component, as the approver would sign it.

prototypes.title: Printed Transmittal and TSR
prototypes.note: The TG03 slip and the TSR, following the real paper form.

prototypes.title: Order Monitoring
prototypes.note: Three ways of showing what needs doing across every order.
